known.title: The append check sets the last existing position to the remote row count minus one and compares with a strict less-than, so a new row directly before the last existing row passes edit.
known.summary: editPlan sets lastRemotePosition to remoteRows.length - 1 (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:902). The check on plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:907 refuses a new row only when index < lastRemotePosition. The index remoteRows.length - 1 is the slot of the last existing row when no row is inserted. A new row at that index stands before the last existing row, but the strict < does not refuse it. The contract says: 'new rows must be appended after every existing row' (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md:293). Plan step guard and Acceptance A1 say the same. Scenario: an ongoing plan has the rows '| 1 | first_step |' and '| 2 | second_step |'. The export puts a new planned row '| 3 | inserted_step |' between them. The new row has index 1, and lastRemotePosition is 1, so edit exits 0 and writes the body with the inserted row. On a plan with one row, a new row above that row (index 0) also passes. Checked with the gh stub of the repository: both edits exited 0. With the fix, both exit 1 with 'inserted between existing rows; new rows append at the end'. The test at scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs:1173-1185 inserts the new row above two existing rows (index 0), so it does not find the error. The correct form finds the index of the last existing row in the incoming table and refuses every new row before it.

known.title: planWorkStarted catches every failure of the issue events read and returns false, so a failed read makes a started plan editable and edit skips the freeze.
known.summary: planWorkStarted (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:451-471) reads the label events of the issue when the plan is drafting or planned. The gh api events call and its JSON parse are in a try block, and the catch returns false (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:458-466). So any failure of the read (network error, HTTP 5xx, rate limit, authentication error, invalid JSON) makes the plan count as not started. editPlan then skips the whole freeze (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:871). The contract says the freeze applies 'Once work starts (irreversibly: when the current phase is neither `drafting` nor `planned`, or label events show that `plan:ongoing` was ever applied)' (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md:290-291). The guards of this file fail closed: 'A truncated or hand-edited sidecar must stop the edit. Treating it as absent would disable the guard exactly when provenance is least trustworthy.' (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:812-813), and 'A local sidecar failure fails closed' (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md:288). The same function still fails on malformed pages (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:467-469), so a failed read gets weaker handling than a malformed reply. Scenario: a plan went ongoing, then blocked, then planned. The events call fails with 'HTTP 502: Bad Gateway'. An export that changes a Status cell from planned to done passes edit, and edit writes the body. Checked with a gh wrapper that fails only the events call: edit exited 0 and the remote body held `done`. With the fix, edit exits 1 with 'gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n>/events failed: HTTP 502: Bad Gateway' and writes nothing.

known.title: repositoryCoordinates now returns owner and repo, but archivePullRequestReferences still reads name, so archive sends name=undefined to the GraphQL query.
known.summary: The diff changes the return shape of repositoryCoordinates (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:343-347) from { owner, name } to { owner, repo }. It updates issueComments (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:440), planWorkStarted (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:457), and associatedPullRequests (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:396, { owner, repo: name }). It does not update archivePullRequestReferences: plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:350 still reads 'const { owner, name } = repositoryCoordinates();'. So name is undefined, and plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:366 passes the field 'name=undefined' to gh api graphql. The query binds it in 'repository(owner:$owner,name:$name)' (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:45). The gh manual says: 'For GraphQL requests, all fields other than `query` and `operationName` are interpreted as GraphQL variables.' Its magic type conversion covers only 'literal values `true`, `false`, `null`, and integer numbers', the placeholders, and values that start with '@' (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_api). So gh sends the string 'undefined' as the repository name, and GitHub looks up the repository '<owner>/undefined'. archive calls this function on every archive run (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:1112), so plan.mjs archive fails for every plan in a real repository. The plan lists the latest-closure behavior of archivePullRequestReferences under Do not touch. The tests do not find the error, because the gh stub finds the issue by number and falls back to the default branch of the fixture repository. Checked with the gh stub: the archive GraphQL call recorded 'owner=DocksDocks name=undefined number=4'. With the fix, it recorded 'name=fixture'.
